environment.orchestrator: docker compose -p ocor-bootstrap (deploy/bootstrap/compose.yaml), same live stack provisioned by the WS-12 chain (OCOR-DEV-0079..0084)
environment.backends_under_test: real OPA (http://127.0.0.1:8181), Keycloak (http://127.0.0.1:8080), OpenBao (http://127.0.0.1:8200), the C6/security-boundary identity/policy control plane
environment.reused_deliverable: ocor_runtime.security.ports (OCOR-DEV-0014, sealed and unmodified) supplies ControlName/ControlStatus/SecurityControlError and the fail-closed require_available contract; scripts/fault_inject_test_environment.py (OCOR-DEV-0083, sealed and unmodified) supplies fault_command/http_reachable/_poll for real container fault injection; this task adds only a bounded-timeout HTTP probe and a correlated audit event around them
environment.ci_provisioning: proactively added real, ephemeral OPA/Keycloak/OpenBao services (all 3 are pre-built pinned images, run via docker run + health-wait, unlike Fuseki which needed a build step) to the same 3 CI workflows already carrying TypeDB and Fuseki, rehearsed locally on alternate ports before being added to any workflow

commands.command: CI provisioning rehearsal: docker run for OPA/OpenBao/Keycloak on alternate host ports (all 3 pre-built pinned images, no build step needed), health-wait, real endpoint verification, teardown -- never touching the live ocor-bootstrap stack

pytest ocor-runtime/tests/tasks/test_ocor_dev_0021.py -v against the real live stack, repeated 4 times to demonstrate determinism (each run performs 2 real pause/unpause fault-injection cycles against opa and openbao)

post-run verification that OPA's loaded policy and OpenBao's ocor/ mount survived the pause/unpause cycles (pause freezes the process, unlike restart which OCOR-DEV-0083 found wipes OPA/Keycloak's ephemeral in-memory state)
full local pytest regression, ocor-runtime/tests/ (OCOR_LIVE_POSTGRES_DSN set locally, pointed at the ocor-bootstrap postgresql service)
full local pytest regression, 3 reports/tests suites

requirement_results.command: a bounded probe against each of OPA, Keycloak and OpenBao while healthy succeeds within its declared timeout and produces an AVAILABLE audit event carrying the exact correlation/causation identifiers passed in

ControlStatus.require_available (sealed, OCOR-DEV-0014) always raises SecurityControlError with a stable {CONTROL}_UNAVAILABLE reason code for an unavailable status, for every control including WORKLOAD_IDENTITY -- a timeout or outage can never be silently treated as a permit

a real bounded pause/unpause fault-injection cycle on OPA: the probe against the paused service is denied within the declared bounded timeout (never hangs), with a CONTROL_TIMEOUT audit event carrying the original correlation/causation identifiers, and succeeds again once OPA is unpaused and recovers
the same real bounded pause/unpause fault-injection cycle on OpenBao

a success probe and a failure probe issued with the identical correlation_id/causation_id both emit an audit event carrying those same identifiers and the same field shape, proving the audit trail never depends on the control having actually answered
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: The bounded-timeout proof relies on a real docker pause, which freezes the target container's process rather than simulating packet loss or a slow-but-not-frozen backend; this is the same real-fault-injection primitive already sealed and reused unmodified from OCOR-DEV-0083, and is a stronger, not weaker, proof that the client-side deadline is honored regardless of the failure's exact shape.

This spike probes control AVAILABILITY (an HTTP health round trip) rather than exercising a full PolicyDecision/AuthenticatedPrincipal/WorkloadIdentity object graph (OCOR-DEV-0014's richer dataclasses, which require additional fields such as session_id/actor_chain out of this spike's scope); ControlStatus.require_available -- the actual fail-closed mechanism -- is exercised directly and unmodified.

This task added real, ephemeral OPA/Keycloak/OpenBao services to the same 3 CI workflows already carrying TypeDB and Fuseki; every future PR now also starts these 3 containers in those jobs. Keycloak in particular takes ~20-30s to become ready, the slowest of the three.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every pause fault-injection test recovers the target service in a finally-equivalent sequence (unpause, then poll for reachability) before the test's own assertions on the failure path run, so a failed assertion still leaves the service recovering; verified directly by the post-run check that OPA's loaded policy and OpenBao's ocor/ mount both survived every pause/unpause cycle across 4 consecutive full test-suite runs, and by the full regression suite passing immediately afterward against the same live stack. The CI provisioning step itself was rehearsed end-to-end locally (start, health-wait, real endpoint check, teardown) on alternate ports before being added to any workflow.
